messages:
anya: Quick sync — I want to run a sensitivity drill for judge selection. Goal: measure consistency when prompts are paraphrased + how quantized judge variants behave. Who can own the test harness and CI gating?
kevin: I can take the harness. Plan: sample N prompts, generate M paraphrases each, run each judge variant (fp16, int8, nf4) and compare scores/rankings.
sophia: Add a human-labeled gold subset (n=200) for agreement and per-slice bias checks (gender, region, dialect). Also track calibration (ECE).
dmitri: Tie-breaker policy question: if two judges disagree, do we prefer the higher-calibrated model or an ensemble consensus? My vote: deterministic pipeline -> ensemble first, then tie-break to human label if ensemble confidence < threshold.
ryan: For CI gating: propose fail conditions: 1) absolute agreement with gold drops > 8% vs baseline, OR 2) ranking Spearman drops below 0.92 on core eval set, OR 3) any demographic slice shows >5% degradation.
anke: (typo) meant kevin : )
kevin: Notes on outputs: harness will dump TSV rows: prompt_id\tparaphrase_id\tjudge_name\tscore\tseed\tquant_mode. We'll compute pairwise disagreement rate and Spearman per-prompt ranking.
kevin: Command prototype:
```
python eval_runner.py --job judge-sensitivity --models judge-1.0,judge-contrast-qlora --paraphrases 5 --quantize fp16,int8,nf4 --out s3://redwood-eval/judge-sensitivity/1769001234.tsv
```
anya: Include an automated bias check step that runs targeted prompt templates (e.g., occupations + gender) and emits slice-level delta vs baseline.
sophia: Also capture KL divergence of score distributions between fp16 and quantized variants per model. If KL > 0.1, flag for manual review.
dmitri: We need a reproducible seed sweep; some judge outputs are noisy. Add 3 seeds per config and report mean+std of disagreement.
ryan: CI wiring: create a GitHub action that triggers harness on PRs to judge config repo. It should post a short summary comment and an artifacts link. Fail-on-thresholds should block merges for major judge swaps.
kevin: I'll add a lightweight visual report (html) showing per-prompt heatmap of pairwise judge score differences + top offending prompts. That helps triage.
eval-bot: preliminary-run complete — ran 1k prompts x5 paraphrases across judge-1.0 (fp16) and judge-contrast-qlora (int8). Summary: disagreement=6.3%, Spearman=0.935, KL(int8||fp16)=0.072. Full TSV: s3://redwood-eval/judge-sensitivity/prelim/1769001234.tsv :eyes:
anya: Nice — disagreement under the 8% gate but keep an eye on the worst-performing prompts. Can we add an automated perturbation where we inject minor typos/punctuation changes to test brittleness?
sophia: Yeah add paraphrase types: lexical, grammatical, punctuation, typos. Score them separately.
dmitri: For tie-breakers: logging needs to keep context hash so we can reproduce exact conversation snippet later. Also store model logits when available for future analysis.
kevin: Will implement logs + an indexing table: (prompt_hash -> s3 paths).
anya: Ownership: kevin leads harness + CI wiring. sophia owns gold-label collection + bias slice definitions. dmitri owns tie-breaker policy + logging schema. ryan owns gating thresholds + GH action. I'll coordinate follow-up and a doc summarizing the acceptance criteria.
ryan: Thanks, assigning PR to kevin. I'll draft the GH action template.
kevin: Starting PR in judge-eval-runner, will include sample TSV and small unit test for paraphrase generator.
sophia: I'll start recruiting labelers for the 200-example gold set and create a quick Google form for initial labels.
eval-bot: scheduled-run created: judge-sensitivity-weekly at 03:00 UTC, artifacts go to s3://redwood-eval/judge-sensitivity/weekly/1769001234/ :memo:
